sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Fayette County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
Deeds for Fayette County property are recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office in the courthouse at 61 E Main Street in Uniontown, PA 15401. The office phone is 724-430-1238 and the fax is 724-430-1458.

Fayette County records go back to 1784, and the county's own FAQ explains that the area belonged to Westmoreland County before that. The same office also records mortgages, releases, satisfaction pieces, plans, powers of attorney, leases, notary bonds and military discharges (DD-214 forms are the one record that is not public).

For a seller, the recorder is the last stop. The deed signed at the closing table becomes the public record of the new owner only once this office stamps it, assigns an instrument number and a volume and page, and prints the recording time on every page.

sections.h2: What hours does the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds keep?
sections.html:
Weekday service runs 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., with the front counter shut from 12 to 1 daily. Recording itself runs 8 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4 p.m., so a deed that arrives during the lunch closure waits for the afternoon session.

  • Office hours: 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed 12 to 1.
  • Recording hours: 8 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Veteran ID program: 10 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 3 p.m.

Anyone sending a Fayette County closing package should plan to arrive well before 4 p.m. and to hold a payment ready, since the county states that all recording fees and transfer taxes are payable at the time of recording.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Fayette County recorder accepts it?
sections.html:
A deed needs a typed parcel number, a proper notary acknowledgment and correct tax paperwork, or it is sent back unrecorded. Fayette County's recording requirements page lists the rules, and most rejections come from small gaps in them.

  • A PIN (the tax assessment parcel number) must be typed on the first page, and the Tax Assessment Office issues a UPI number for it before the document is recorded.
  • The acknowledgment must name the county, state and date, the person or corporate officer appearing, and carry the notary's signature and commission expiration date. The acknowledgment date cannot come before the date of the document. An embossed seal is now optional.
  • The deed must name the municipality, county and state where the land sits.
  • The written dollar amount must match the numerals on every deed and mortgage.
  • Grantee, mortgagee and assignee need a mailing address with ZIP code.
  • Any document that points back to an earlier mortgage must cite its book and page numbers, not a document number alone.
  • A re-recorded document has to explain why it is being recorded again.

Typing or writing on a notary stamp is a violation of the Pennsylvania notary law according to the county, so a stamp that is smudged or altered is a common reason for a bounce. Every document also needs a printed name so it can be returned to the right attorney or title company, along with a self-addressed stamped envelope unless the office holds it for pickup.

sections.h2: What will the recorder charge for a Fayette County deed?
sections.html:
The total depends on the base fee for the document type plus add-ons, and the office will quote the current deed figure by phone at 724-430-1238. The fee schedule on the county website, last dated June 28, 2023, lists the add-ons that apply to a typical home sale.

Fayette County Recorder of Deeds add-on fees
ItemAmount
UPI fee, per PIN number$20.00
Each page over 4$2.00
Each name over 4 (indexing)$0.50
Extra marginal notation$2.00
Copies in the office, per page$0.50
Copies by mail, per page$1.00
Certified copy$3.00 plus the copy cost

Source: Fayette County Recorder of Deeds fee schedule PDF and recorder FAQ on fayettecountypa.org.

A parcel-by-parcel UPI charge matters on rural sales. A farm assembled from three tax parcels needs three PIN numbers certified, so the UPI line alone reaches $60 before the base fee.

sections.h2: How is realty transfer tax paid on a Fayette County sale?
sections.html:
The county's recording requirements say recording fees and realty transfer tax can go in one check made out to Fayette County Recorder of Deeds. The fee schedule describes the transfer tax as 1% state plus 1% local.

The deed has to state the price paid, or it must carry a Statement of Value that explains why no tax is due. An original goes into the document as a page and a duplicate goes to the state. Questions about the tax can be emailed to the Department of Revenue realty transfer tax division at ra-bitrealtytransfertax@pa.gov.

When a property lies in more than one local taxing district, the deed must show whole-number percentages for the division of the local share. The state's own page confirms that buyer and seller are both liable and that the recorder passes the 1% to the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: How do you search Fayette County land records?
sections.html:
Index searches for most documents from 1950 to the present are free through the US Land Records site, while images are pay-per-access. Documents recorded before January 1, 2001 are also kept in books in the office, and public search stations in the Uniontown courthouse show the rest.

The recorder indexes by name, with the legal description and municipality, and not by street address. For an address or parcel lookup, the county sends people to the Tax Assessment property search or the Mapping Room, reachable at 724-430-1350, extension 229.

  • Archive Viewer indexes cover deeds and mortgages from 1950 to 1974, plans from 1791 to 1988 and agreements from 1854 to 1949.
  • Liens and judgments are not filed here. The Prothonotary on the first floor of the courthouse handles them at 724-430-1272.
  • Subdivision plans are recorded in this office, while zoning questions go to Planning, Zoning and Community Development on the fourth floor at 724-430-1210.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about selling a house in Fayette County?
sections.html:
Fayette County has 790.76 square miles of land and an estimated 123,021 residents in 2025, down 4.5% from the April 2020 base, according to Census QuickFacts. Owners occupy 72.4% of homes, and the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $143,200.

Median household income is $58,236 and 14.7% of residents live in poverty. Only 196 building permits were issued in 2025, so little new construction competes with resale houses. The county was part of Westmoreland until 1783 and grew on coal, coke and steel, and the Census also shows a median gross rent of $793 for owners weighing a rental instead of a sale.

Uniontown, where the courthouse stands, anchors the county, and the National Road, the Monongahela and Youghiogheny valleys and the Connellsville Amtrak stop shape where homes cluster. A seller who wants a quick closing in Fayette County mainly needs a clean deed, a certified parcel number and a buyer whose title agent knows the Uniontown office schedule.

faqs.q: How much is the UPI fee in Fayette County?
faqs.a: The posted schedule shows $20.00 for each PIN number certified. A deed that covers two tax parcels therefore adds $40.00 to the recording bill.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Fayette County without a parcel number?
faqs.a: No. The county requires a PIN typed on the first page, and the Tax Assessment Office issues the UPI number before recording. A deed without it comes back unrecorded.

faqs.q: Can one check cover the recording fee and transfer tax in Fayette County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's recording requirements allow fees and realty transfer tax in a single check payable to Fayette County Recorder of Deeds, as long as the amount is exact.

faqs.q: Does the Fayette County recorder search for liens?
faqs.a: No. The recorder does not file liens or judgments. Those go through the Prothonotary's office in the courthouse at 724-430-1272, while the recorder shows mortgages and whether they were satisfied.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my recorded deed in Fayette County?
faqs.a: Visit the Uniontown office, where copies are $0.50 per page, or find the document through the US Land Records index. A certified copy costs $0.50 per page plus $3.00 for the certification.
